headline: Majors sit above their 200-day lines, but the tape is resting, not accelerating
paragraphs: The regime is straightforward for five of the seven majors: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all sit above their 200-day averages with golden crosses in place, the classic marker of an uptrend that's been running long enough to reorganize the moving averages in its favor. DOGE and ADA are the outliers, both below their 200-day lines with no golden cross, and both showing the worst 12-month drawdowns of the group (-70.4% and -77.5% from their highs, respectively). That split matters: this isn't a market where everything is one trade. Bitcoin itself is 37.5% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, which is a useful reminder that 'above the 200-day' and 'near the highs' are two different claims.

Momentum is where the story gets interesting, because it's quietly out of step with trend. Every single asset in the board shows MACD below signal, even the ones in confirmed uptrends. RSI readings cluster in the mid-50s to low-60s (BTC 57.0, ETH 60.6, SOL 57.6, XRP 58.1, BNB 55.9), which is neutral-to-firm, not overheated, not weak. Put together: this is a market catching its breath inside an intact uptrend, not one rolling over. The 30-day changes are the real tell of how far things have run, up 22.9% to 39.6% across the majors, while the 7-day changes have gone flat or negative (BNB down 6.1% on the week, DOGE down 6.7%, ADA down 4.7%). Fast money paused; the month's gains are still on the board.

Positioning leans long but isn't stretched. BTC funding sits at an annualized 3.4%, ETH at 6.0%, both modest costs for holding a long perpetual position. Funding is the fee longs pay shorts (or vice versa) every eight hours to keep the perpetual price tethered to spot; low positive funding means longs are paying a small toll, not desperate to stay in the trade. SOL and XRP funding run hotter at 11% annualized with long/short ratios of 1.88 and 2.09, and the liquidation tape backs that up: SOL saw $449,603 in short liquidations against $103,197 in longs over 4 hours, XRP saw $854,195 in shorts wiped against $315,839 in longs. Shorts are getting squeezed in the higher-beta names while BTC and ETH open interest ($2.05B and $1.51B respectively) sits comparatively calm.

Flows tell a mixed story depending on which clock you use. BTC ETFs printed a $9.7M inflow on 14 Sep 2026, but the five-session net is a $453.0M outflow, a clear case where the daily print and the short trend disagree. ETH ETFs are cleaner: $216.4M in on 11 Sep 2026 against a $222.8M five-session net, same direction both ways. Whale activity over the trailing 72 hours nets to exactly zero, but the biggest single moves were $170.8M in USDC onto Kraken and $157.1M in USDT onto Binance, stablecoins headed toward exchanges, which usually reads as buying power getting staged rather than assets being sold. The weekly whale series backs a moving-onto-exchanges bias in three of the last four weeks (Aug 25: $1,258M onto exchanges; Sep 01: $479M onto exchanges; Sep 15: $725M onto exchanges), with only the Sep 08 week showing $347M moving off. Stablecoin float itself is up a modest 1.25% over 30 days to $310.1B, dry powder growing slowly, not surging.

Sentiment sits at 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 31 to 74. That's a crowd feeling good while the tape underneath shows cooling weekly momentum, MACD rolling under signal across the board, and a net-zero whale flow with more stablecoins parked on exchanges than off. It's not a contradiction that screams reversal, just a gap between mood and mechanics worth naming. Worth watching from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF outflow turns into a same-direction run, whether funding on SOL and XRP cools from its current 11% annualized pace as the short squeeze works through, and whether MACD crosses back above signal in BTC and ETH, which would put momentum back in agreement with the 200-day trend structure that's currently intact but unconfirmed by the shorter-term signals.
